have hs : (∑ j, (p j)⁻¹)⁻¹ = 2 := by
    rw [← Finset.add_sum_erase Finset.univ (fun j => (p j)⁻¹) (Finset.mem_univ i)]
    have he : ∑ j ∈ Finset.univ.erase i, (p j)⁻¹ = 0 := by
      apply Finset.sum_eq_zero
      intro j hj
      simp [p,(Finset.mem_erase.mp hj).1]
    simp [he,p]
findings.problem: The reciprocal sum is supported only at i, but the proof manually separates that index and proves an auxiliary erased sum vanishes. The conditional-sum simplification already expresses this calculation directly.
findings.proposed_change:
Replace this block with:
  have hs : (∑ j, (p j)⁻¹)⁻¹ = 2 := by
    -- Only the distinguished index contributes.
    simp [p, apply_ite]
findings.benefit: Removes the erased-finset bookkeeping while keeping the key mathematical observation explicit. This also handles singleton κ directly; an empty κ is impossible because i : κ is supplied.

have hzero (i : κ) : trimWord (s i) = [] := by
    apply List.length_eq_zero_iff.mp
    exact Nat.eq_zero_of_le_zero (hm ▸ Finset.single_le_sum (f:=fun i => (trimWord (s i)).length) (fun _ _ => Nat.zero_le _) (Finset.mem_univ i))
findings.problem: The proof derives each zero length through an inequality and equality transport. For natural-number summands, Finset.sum_eq_zero_iff gives the required conclusion directly.
findings.proposed_change:
Replace this block with:
  have hzero (i : κ) : trimWord (s i) = [] := by
    apply List.length_eq_zero_iff.mp
    exact Finset.sum_eq_zero_iff.mp hm i (Finset.mem_univ i)
findings.benefit: States the mathematical reasoning directly: a sum of natural numbers is zero only when every summand is zero. It removes the intermediate inequality without changing the zero-length cases.
